assertions.name: phase decorrelation does NOT amplify the tail: the scramble ratio s_n = sup|u_n|(scrambled)/sup|u_n|(coherent) <= 1 on every excited tail rung, at both cadences (every-step and 0.1-eddy) and every eps — the coherent evolution is the in-model worst case, so the SF arc's fully-coherent real-amplitude models are CONSERVATIVE with respect to sweeping/decorrelation, and SF10's cross-model amplification is attributable to triad structure, not phase coherence
assertions.source: max s_n per (cadence, eps) over tail rungs excited in both runs; deterministic hash phases, moduli untouched

assertions.name: the modulus damped-forced form (rung_equilibrium_forced instance) holds on the SCRAMBLED runs too: r_n <= 1 on every excited empty-start rung — the Lean-backed route is phase-insensitive, as the triangle bound predicts
assertions.source: max r_n per (cadence, eps) on scrambled runs

description: SF11 (bean qou-ougq): isolates the phase effect from SF10's triad-structure confound by comparing the complex Sabra q-shell against itself with deterministically hash-scrambled phases (moduli untouched, energy preserved by the scramble) at two cadences. s_n <= 1 means decorrelation weakens tail excitation and the coherent model is the worst case. Scope (a); float64 complex RK2 exploratory tier; sweeping in full NS also advects structures spatially, which no shell model represents — the residual caveat, now narrowed to spatial advection only.
